thread:
oncall-bot: Pager: serving-pool 'dedicated-west-3' reporting repeated model load failures on warmup — multiple containers crashed during initialization, elevated error rate to 6% and increased cold-start latency. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

Maria G: I see errors in the warmup job logs, OOM happens during model deserialization. Not a steady-state OOM, it fails while loading weights.

Ashok P: Can you paste the exact stack from the worker? Also which model variant is this (fp16/8/quant)?

Maria G: It's the rdx-large-quant8 variant we rolled out for cost testing. Log snippet:```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] ERROR load_model: deserialization failed: unexpected end of stream
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] INFO alloc: requesting 12.4G GPU memory
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] ERROR cuda: cudaDriverError 4: too many resources requested for launch
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] FATAL worker: process exited (signal 9)
```

Dani L: Interesting — deserialization failure + cuda launch errors. Could be a corrupted model shard or we hit a kernel/memory combination that spikes during deserial.

Eng-Runtime: We're seeing the same across 3 nodes in the pool. All are nvidia-a100-40g. Memory accounting shows a transient spike during mapping of large weights. The runtime's prefetcher allocates pinned buffers, then kernels try to initialize cuBLAS handles which pushes simultaneous GPU allocations.

SRE Bot: Automated mitigation suggestions: 1) drain new warmups to minimum concurrency, 2) fallback to cpu-warmup path for affected nodes, 3) roll back to previous quantization profile. Would you like me to run the mitigation?

Maria G: Initiating manual interventions first. @Kai R can you drain the warmup queue for dedicated-west-3? Limit concurrent model loads to 2.

Kai R: On it. Command used:```bash
# reduce warmup concurrency
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-west-3 --warmup-concurrency 2
# drain new warmups
redwoodctl pools drain-warmup --pool dedicated-west-3 --reason "hotfix: deserialization failures"
```
Backfill traffic should still hit the stable pool.

Ashok P: I'm going to trigger a fallback to the fp16 variant (less aggressive quant) for the canary route and pause the new quant8 rollout. Executing:```bash
redwoodctl routes update canary-route --model rdx-large-fp16 --traffic 100
```

Product-Support: Heads-up — two paying Dedicated customers in us-west experienced elevated 503s for ~7 minutes. I've opened a ticket and notified them we have a mitigation plan and will provide RCA.

Dani L: For debugging we should capture the exact model file checksums on the failing nodes and compare with object storage. Also dump /var/log/nv* and the process core if possible.

Eng-Runtime: I pulled checksums, one shard shows different CRC compared to S3: bad shard at offset ~2.1G. Possible partial upload or storage corruption during a previous push. That would explain the deserialization "unexpected end of stream".

Maria G: If it's a corrupted shard, that matches the pattern. But why CUDA launch errors? Maybe the runtime retries and attempts to initialize kernels with malformed data, causing invalid memory accesses, then oom/kills.

SRE Bot: Suggestion: mark the model build as tainted and stop warmups until we replace shards. Would you like me to update model state?

Kai R: I've updated the model catalog entry to 'tainted' and removed canary routing for quant8. Command:```bash
redwoodctl models set-state rdx-large-quant8 --state tainted --note "corrupted shard detected 2026-03-10"
```

Ashok P: I'll re-push a cleaned build of the quant8 artifacts from the build farm and run integrity checks on upload. ETA ~25m. Meanwhile, we should free the nodes that crashed and clear restart backoff.

Eng-Runtime: Restarting the affected containers now and clearing GPU cache. Commands run:```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/worker-dedicated-west-3
docker-compose exec worker /bin/bash -c "echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches"
# clear CUDA context on freed nodes via driver reset (coord with infra)
```
Nodes came back but warmups are paused.

Maria G: Monitoring metrics: error rate dropped from 6% to 0.7% after draining and fallback. Latency for cold starts dropped ~40%. Good temporary improvement.

Product-Support: Notifying customers that we mitigated and working on replace + fix. Will send incident summary after root cause completes.

Dani L: Next steps for RCA: 1) verify artifact pipeline (CI->storage) checksums and add a preflight integrity validation, 2) make warmup deserialization resilient (validate chunk sizes before mapping), 3) add a guarded fallback so corrupted shards don't trigger kernel initializations.

Kai R: I'll file infra ticket to add object-store health checks and S3 signed-checksum validation in the uploader.

SRE Bot: If no objections, I'll set a temporary alert to detect deserialization checksum mismatch and escalate to eng-runtime.

Maria G: Do it. Also schedule a follow-up postmortem with eng-runtime + infra + build farm. I'll take lead on the write-up.

Ashok P: Re-push succeeded. Validated CRCs, re-enabled fp16 then will re-run quant8 rollout behind canary with extra integrity checks.

Eng-Runtime: Confirming warmup re-enable plan: incremental canary (1 instance), strict preflight -> run for 30m -> increase. We'll keep warmup-concurrency=2 for another 2 hours.

Product-Support: Customer update sent. No immediate SLA credits requested yet.

SRE Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Documented timeline and actions in incident tracker: #INC-2026-0310-05.

Dani L: Handoff: I'll take the next 45m watch to observe metric regressions and follow up with postmortem notes. @Kai R please join if any infra restarts are needed.

Kai R: I'll remain available for the handoff.

Maria G: Thanks team. I'll draft the RCA and attach logs + checksums. Closing thread unless new errors surface. :white_check_mark:
